rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-eight builder trees go (a row of corals and torrey pines every 6 m along the back fences, queen and fan palms 3-4.7 m from the houses, others in the yards); seven come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the picnic table, the grill, the adirondack chairs, on the open lot corner, and one each on the old back fence row and in a back yard.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m east, 13 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the big open lot corner, 32 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the back yard with the gas grill and the adirondack chair: a magnolia over both
the next yard's two white adirondack chairs: a jacaranda over them
the north back yard, 8 m from the house: the yard's tree
the north back fence row, 34 m east: the row's one tree (it had one every 6 m)
